section: Inflation - types, causes, measurement (CPI, WPI, core inflation), effects and control measures
subsections: Price indices - publisher, base year, weights
Index used for measuring inflation - headline measure and the switch
Relative ordering of food, headline and core inflation

accepted.s: The CPI (Rural/Urban/Combined) in India is published by which organisation?
o: National Statistical Office, Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT
accepted.x: The CPI for Rural, Urban and Combined sectors is published by the National Statistical Office under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.
accepted.tq: Identify the institution associated with the index rather than confusing it with the WPI publisher.
accepted.sec: Price indices - publisher, base year, weights

accepted.s: The current base year of the new CPI (Rural/Urban/Combined) series is
accepted.x: The new CPI series uses 2024 as its base year and was introduced from the earlier 2012-based series.
accepted.tq: Use the latest base year and distinguish it from the earlier CPI series.
accepted.sec: Price indices - publisher, base year, weights

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the new CPI series:
1. Its weights are derived from the Household Consumption Expenditure Survey 2023-24.
2. It has 12 divisions based on COICOP 2018.
3. The earlier CPI structure had six groups.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: the new CPI uses HCES 2023-24 weights, follows 12 COICOP 2018 divisions and replaces the earlier six-group structure.
accepted.tq: Check whether all the structural changes belong to the same revised index series.
accepted.sec: Price indices - publisher, base year, weights

accepted.s: How many items are included in the new CPI basket, and how are they divided between goods and services?
accepted.x: The new CPI basket contains 358 items, comprising 308 goods and 50 services.
accepted.tq: Match the total with its component figures before selecting the numerical option.
accepted.sec: Price indices - publisher, base year, weights

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly states the weights of food and beverages and housing in the new CPI basket?
accepted.x: Food and beverages have a weight of 36.75% and housing has a weight of 17.67% in the new CPI basket.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely related percentage figures and their categories.
accepted.sec: Price indices - publisher, base year, weights

accepted.s: Which of the following features was added to the new CPI series?
o: Services were removed from the basket
Rural house rent and 12 online platforms
Urban house rent and 12 manufacturing groups
accepted.x: Rural house rent and 12 online platforms were added to the new CPI series.
accepted.tq: Select the precise combination of additions instead of an extreme or reversed statement.
accepted.sec: Price indices - publisher, base year, weights

accepted.s: The current base year of the Wholesale Price Index series is
accepted.x: The current WPI series has 2022-23 as its base year and replaced the earlier 2011-12 base.
accepted.tq: Separate the current base year from an earlier officially used base year.
accepted.sec: Price indices - publisher, base year, weights

accepted.s:
With reference to the new WPI series, consider the following statements:
1. It contains 957 items.
2. The earlier series contained 697 items.
3. Its weights are based on Gross Value of Output.
4. It covers services along with goods.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because WPI covers goods and does not cover services.
accepted.tq: Find the single false statement by testing the coverage of the index separately from its numerical details.
accepted.sec: Price indices - publisher, base year, weights

accepted.s: The proposed relationship between the new WPI and the Producer Price Index is that
o: PPI will run alongside WPI for five years, after which WPI will be phased out
WPI will cover services only after PPI is introduced
Both indices will be permanently merged after one year
accepted.x: The new WPI is intended to run with a new Producer Price Index for five years, after which WPI is to be phased out.
accepted.tq: Follow the stated sequence of transition instead of reversing the roles of the two indices.
accepted.sec: Price indices - publisher, base year, weights

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: GDP deflator — Office of the Economic Adviser — 2022-23 base
accepted.x: CPI-IW is published by the Labour Bureau and uses 2016 as its base year. The other pairs incorrectly combine publishers or base years.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure publisher-base pair and eliminate crossed combinations.
accepted.sec: Price indices - publisher, base year, weights

accepted.s: The CPI-IW series with 2016 as its base year has been in use since
accepted.x: The CPI-IW has used the 2016 base since September 2020; the preceding base was 2001.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the effective date of a series from the date of a later CPI revision.
accepted.sec: Price indices - publisher, base year, weights

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding CPI-AL and CPI-RL is correct?
o: CPI-AL has a 2011-12 base, whereas CPI-RL has a 2022-23 base.
CPI-AL has a 2019 base from June 2025, whereas CPI-RL is listed with the 1986-87 base.
CPI-AL is published by NSO and CPI-RL by DPIIT.
Both CPI-AL and CPI-RL have a 2024 base from February 2026.
accepted.x: CPI-AL moved to a 2019 base from June 2025, while CPI-RL is listed with the 1986-87 base. Both are published by the Labour Bureau.
accepted.tq: Separate the two similar labour-sector indices by their stated base years.
accepted.sec: Price indices - publisher, base year, weights

accepted.s: The linking factor for CPI-AL is stated as
o: 10.72 for both Andhra Pradesh and India
10.72 for India and 9.69 for Andhra Pradesh
9.69 for Andhra Pradesh and 10.72 for India
10.72 for Andhra Pradesh and 9.69 for India
accepted.x: The linking factor for CPI-AL is 10.72 for Andhra Pradesh and 9.69 for India.
accepted.tq: Read the geographical labels carefully before matching each figure.
accepted.sec: Price indices - publisher, base year, weights

accepted.s: CPI-IW is primarily used for determining the dearness allowance of
accepted.x: CPI-IW is used for determining dearness allowance for industrial workers.
accepted.tq: Link the specialised index to the category of workers it represents.
accepted.sec: Price indices - publisher, base year, weights

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly compares CPI and WPI?
o: CPI measures producer prices of goods only, whereas WPI measures retail prices of goods and services.
CPI measures retail prices of goods and services, whereas WPI measures first-point bulk sale prices of goods only.
Both CPI and WPI measure only retail prices of goods.
Both CPI and WPI include services with identical weights.
accepted.x: CPI measures consumer retail prices and includes goods and services. WPI measures first-point bulk sale or producer-level prices and covers goods only.
accepted.tq: Split the comparison into price level and coverage before choosing the complete pair.
accepted.sec: Price indices - publisher, base year, weights

accepted.s: Which index is regarded as the broadest measure because it covers all goods and services produced in the economy?
accepted.x: The GDP deflator is the broadest measure because it covers all goods and services produced in the economy, including services.
accepted.tq: Use the coverage clue to distinguish the economy-wide deflator from price-basket indices.
accepted.sec: Price indices - publisher, base year, weights

accepted.s: The GDP deflator is calculated as
o: Real GDP multiplied by nominal GDP divided by 100
Nominal GDP divided by real GDP multiplied by 100
Nominal GDP minus real GDP divided by 100
Real GDP divided by nominal GDP multiplied by 100
accepted.x: GDP deflator equals nominal GDP divided by real GDP, multiplied by 100. A rise in the deflator reduces the purchasing power of money.
accepted.tq: Recall the numerator-denominator order in the formula rather than reversing it.
accepted.sec: Price indices - publisher, base year, weights

accepted.s: A rise in the GDP deflator, other things remaining the same, indicates a reduction in the
accepted.x: An increase in the GDP deflator reflects a rise in the general price level and therefore reduces the purchasing power of money.
accepted.tq: Translate the movement of a price index into its effect on money value.
accepted.sec: Price indices - publisher, base year, weights

accepted.s:
Arrange the following developments in the correct chronological order:
A. RBI adopted CPI (Combined) as its key inflation measure
B. Monetary Policy Framework Agreement
C. Amendment of the RBI Act providing the statutory framework
D. First invocation of the report requirement after breach of the inflation band
accepted.x: The sequence is CPI adoption in April 2014, the February 2015 Monetary Policy Framework Agreement, the 2016 RBI Act amendment and the first invocation in 2022.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest event and then place the agreement, legislation and later invocation.
accepted.sec: Index used for measuring inflation - headline measure and the switch

accepted.s: Before the adoption of CPI (Combined) by the RBI in April 2014, India used which index as the headline inflation measure?
accepted.x: WPI was earlier used as India's headline inflation measure. The RBI adopted CPI (Combined) as its key measure in April 2014 following the Urjit Patel Committee framework.
accepted.tq: Test the before-and-after distinction in a policy transition.
accepted.sec: Index used for measuring inflation - headline measure and the switch

accepted.s: Which of the following provisions is correctly matched with the RBI Act, 1934 as amended in 2016?
o: Section 45ZA — constitution of the six-member MPC
Section 45ZB — inflation target fixed by the Centre with RBI every five years
Section 45ZN — report to be made when the inflation band is breached for three consecutive quarters
accepted.x: Section 45ZN requires a report when the inflation band is breached for three consecutive quarters. Section 45ZA concerns the target-setting process, while Section 45ZB concerns the MPC.
accepted.tq: Match each statutory section with its specific function instead of relying on the common subject matter.
accepted.sec: Index used for measuring inflation - headline measure and the switch

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about India's flexible inflation-targeting framework:
1. The inflation target is fixed by the Centre in consultation with the RBI every five years.
2. The Monetary Policy Committee consists of six members.
3. A breach of the tolerance band for three consecutive quarters requires the RBI to report its reasons to the Government.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements correctly describe the flexible inflation-targeting framework under the amended RBI Act.
accepted.tq: Check the target-setting, MPC composition and breach-reporting provisions together.
accepted.sec: Index used for measuring inflation - headline measure and the switch

accepted.s: For the period from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031, the CPI-based inflation target is
accepted.x: The retained target is 4% with a tolerance band of plus or minus 2% for 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the central target from the width of the tolerance band.
accepted.sec: Index used for measuring inflation - headline measure and the switch

accepted.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with its principal use?
o: CPI — contract escalation only; WPI — dearness allowance only
CPI — dearness allowance; WPI — contract escalation and industrial analysis
CPI-IW — Producer Price Index; WPI — rural wage revision only
GDP deflator — industrial workers' dearness allowance; CPI — producer prices
accepted.x: CPI is also used for dearness allowance, while WPI is used for contract escalation and industrial analysis.
accepted.tq: Associate each index with its practical institutional use without reversing the pair.
accepted.sec: Index used for measuring inflation - headline measure and the switch

accepted.s: Which statement best reflects the policy debate concerning the inflation target?
o: The debate concerns only the choice between WPI and GDP deflator.
Core inflation is stickier and responds more to policy, leading to debate over whether the target should be headline or core inflation.
Headline inflation excludes food and energy, while core inflation includes them.
Core inflation is more volatile than headline inflation and responds less to policy.
accepted.x: The debate is whether policy should target headline or core inflation; core inflation is considered stickier and more responsive to policy.
accepted.tq: Choose the option that states both the nature of core inflation and the actual policy issue.
accepted.sec: Index used for measuring inflation - headline measure and the switch

accepted.s: In May 2026, the relative ordering of food, headline and core inflation was
accepted.x: In May 2026, food inflation was 4.85%, headline inflation was 3.93% and core inflation was 3.73%, giving the order Food > Headline > Core.
accepted.tq: Arrange the three measures by comparing their actual percentages.
accepted.sec: Relative ordering of food, headline and core inflation

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the inflation figures for May 2026 under the new CPI series?
accepted.x: The May 2026 figures were 3.93% headline inflation, 4.85% food inflation and 3.73% core inflation.
accepted.tq: Keep the indicator labels attached to the figures when comparing close percentages.
accepted.sec: Relative ordering of food, headline and core inflation

accepted.s: The first breach of the 4% CPI inflation target in the new series occurred in
accepted.x: Headline CPI inflation reached 4.38% in June 2026, marking the first breach of the 4% target.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the first threshold breach from later higher readings.
accepted.sec: Relative ordering of food, headline and core inflation

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding July 2026 inflation is correct?
o: Headline CPI inflation was 4.45%, rural food inflation was 5.79%, and core inflation was below 3% excluding precious metals.
Headline CPI inflation was 3.93%, rural food inflation was 4.85%, and core inflation exceeded 5%.
Headline CPI inflation was 4.38%, rural food inflation was 5.05%, and core inflation was exactly 4%.
Headline CPI inflation was 4.80%, rural food inflation was 5.70%, and core inflation was above 4.45%.
accepted.x: In July 2026, headline CPI inflation was 4.45%, rural food inflation was 5.79%, and core inflation was below 3% when precious metals were excluded.
accepted.tq: Match the month with all three indicators and reject figures belonging to adjacent months.
accepted.sec: Relative ordering of food, headline and core inflation

accepted.s: Headline CPI inflation reached a 20-month high of 4.8% in
accepted.x: Headline CPI inflation reached 4.8% in August 2026, described as a 20-month high.
accepted.tq: Use the time descriptor to identify the correct monthly observation.
accepted.sec: Relative ordering of food, headline and core inflation

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the inflation position during 2025?
o: CPI inflation was 1.7%, while food inflation was minus 0.2%.
CPI inflation was 3.88%, while food inflation was 2.2%.
CPI inflation was 2.2%, a 12-year low, while food inflation was minus 0.2%.
CPI inflation was 6.7%, while food inflation was 2.2%.
accepted.x: In 2025, CPI inflation was 2.2%, a 12-year low, and food inflation was −0.2%.
accepted.tq: Separate the annual figures from the later financial-year and WPI figures.
accepted.sec: Relative ordering of food, headline and core inflation

accepted.s: The order of inflation measures recorded for 2025 was
accepted.x: For 2025, the stated order was Core > Headline > Food, with headline CPI at 2.2% and food inflation at −0.2%.
accepted.tq: Use the negative food-inflation figure to place food at the end of the order.
accepted.sec: Relative ordering of food, headline and core inflation

accepted.s: Food inflation of −0.2% in 2025 was described as
accepted.x: The −0.2% food inflation recorded in 2025 was described as the first food deflation since 2014.
accepted.tq: Treat the reference year as a separate chronological fact rather than confusing it with the CPI base year.
accepted.sec: Relative ordering of food, headline and core inflation

accepted.s: The lowest CPI inflation recorded in October 2025 was
o: 1.7%, the lowest in the financial year
accepted.x: CPI inflation was 0.3% in October 2025, the lowest recorded in the 2012 series.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the monthly low from the annual low and from the series base year.
accepted.sec: Relative ordering of food, headline and core inflation

accepted.s: According to the Economic Survey 2025-26 figures, CPI inflation fell from 6.7% in FY23 to what level during April–December FY26?
accepted.x: The CPI inflation rate fell from 6.7% in FY23 to 1.7% during April–December FY26.
accepted.tq: Identify the period attached to the figure instead of selecting the nearby annual or WPI rate.
accepted.sec: Relative ordering of food, headline and core inflation

accepted.s: The WPI inflation rate reached a 38-month high of 3.88% in
accepted.x: WPI inflation rose to a 38-month high of 3.88% in March 2026.
accepted.tq: Separate the WPI observation from the monthly CPI observations of June to August.
accepted.sec: Relative ordering of food, headline and core inflation

accepted.s: Which explanation was given for WPI inflation being far above CPI inflation in June and July 2026?
o: The inclusion of services in the WPI basket
Higher fuel costs associated with the West Asia conflict
A change in the CPI base year alone
A sharp fall in manufactured-goods prices due to domestic oversupply
accepted.x: WPI inflation was 9.87% in June and 9.78% in July 2026, far above CPI inflation mainly because of fuel costs associated with the West Asia conflict.
accepted.tq: Link the observed divergence between indices to the stated sector-specific cause.
accepted.sec: Relative ordering of food, headline and core inflation

accepted.s: The WPI inflation rates for June and July 2026 were, respectively
accepted.x: WPI inflation was 9.87% in June 2026 and 9.78% in July 2026.
accepted.tq: Preserve the month-wise order when two close numerical values are given.
accepted.sec: Relative ordering of food, headline and core inflation
